Couldn't give them any bigger recommendation for a veterinarian and care service. Thank you.

We went to the Urgent Care on what turned out to be one of the worst days we’ve had in a very long time. Our senior kitty was sick, and after calling around to a few other urgent care clinics Riverbend told us to come right in. When we got there the staff took him immediately to the back and they put us in a private room. After some waiting, some testing and lots of conversations we had to make the difficult decision to put our cat to sleep.

Everyone at Riverbend was kind, compassionate and empathetic. The veterinarian was honestly one of the best I’ve ever seen, and we’ve seen a lot over the years. Their first concern was my cat and his comfort. We’ve visited other Urgent Care’s in the past and Riverbend was a much better experience (even though it ended terribly).

The cost wasn’t bad at all, either. We had bloodwork, ultrasound, medications and some other stuff and we were expecting it to cost way more than it did. Even with the cremation package we chose, I do think their pricing is very reasonable.

I absolutely recommend this place if you’re in the unfortunate circumstance of needing an urgent care vet. If we ever need these kind of services again I know we won’t even bother with the other places. They served us and our cat, Jenkins, very well. I appreciated their genuine care and concern.

My cat had a mild eye infection a month and a half ago and I am finally getting around to doing a review. I was unable to take her in due to a medical condition so my partner had been tasked with this part while I was the one who called around to make the appointment.
Our regular vet was all booked up so they were unable to get her in to see her within a day or two and I didn't feel comfortable waiting any longer to have her seen with her eye issue. I am grateful I found Riverbend searching on Google because they are pretty close to where we live! I called them and talked with the nicest person getting all the needed information and her explaining to me the process and how they operate. It was super easy to schedule an appointment with them and they were flexible and had lots of time slots open which I was kind of surprised because it was last minute on a Friday afternoon. I paid a deposit online to hold her spot and off she and my partner went to their clinic.
I am SO glad we found them and I would not hesitate to take my cats there again for an emergency that needed attention during the hours they are open. My partner reported that Dr. Rupert was really kind and caring and they wrote a really sweet note on our itemized billing and care paperwork that said she was a good patient. This is especially kind because Saphira has a lot of anxiety and I didn't have time to sedate her before her appointment like I do when she goes for regular checkups. I think the price for the exam was pretty reasonable and less than if she were to go to one of the 24 hour clinics in Portland. They also explained everything step by step and what costs were associated so there were NO surprise costs involved and they gave us options. Anyway, I just wanted to say thanks to the team for being so kind to us and taking care of our Saphira.

what can I say about PVWC? How many characters do I get?  The staff are some of the most kind people I’ve ever met at any vet clinic.  I’ve been taking my 3 (now senior) pets to PVWC for over 4 years and they are the only vet clinic I truly trust with the well-being of my kiddos (and the list of people I trust with my babies is short).  We’ve seen different vets over the 4 years here, all have been amazing.  The clinic is very understanding of financial burdens and do their best to work with me on my (never ending) bills (I have older kiddos who have health problems).

Special shoutout to Dr. Erickson who always takes the time to explain things to me, without judgement; she’s very patient.  Jay is absolutely amazing — truly such a lovely human — I’ve never not seen Jay with a real smile and warmth that you can feel as soon as you walk into the clinic.

To further expand on the clinic’s kindness, my pitty (who was there to get sutures removed post cancer surgery) and it was her birthday so I brought cupcakes for the staff and my pitty wore her favorite tutu.  The staff (many of whom know my pitty well as she’s there often for her various health issues), all came out from their busy clinic day to come wish her a happy 11th birthday and give her some pets and love (see the photo attached).

if you are looking for a vet clinic that you can truly trust to take incredible care of your pet(s), look no further.

I am forever grateful to PVWC for the care they provide to my pets (and to me as the parent).

My family and I have brought dogs here since the 1980s. Every Fremont vet we've seen has been knowledgeable, caring, and helpful. The support staff goes above and beyond my expectations, as well.

They are a busy clinic, and sometimes get walk-in emergencies, so I've found it's best to schedule as ahead of time as you can. I’ve been here a few times in the past 5 years for 3 different bunnies but had the best experience last night / this morning.

Two of my bunnies got in a scuffle yesterday late afternoon and one ended up with a wound that didn’t look like it would heal on its own. He got vitals taken not long after we arrived and the vet on duty saw him about 2 hours after we got checked in, which is pretty reasonable for Dove Lewis or any ER vet really.

I have lots of praise to say for Dr. Hilfman specifically. He was kind, confident and direct about what he recommended for care. He and the other staff accommodated our request to let us feed our bunny some hay and critical care prior to leaving him there overnight. It meant so much that me and my partner get some calories in his belly because he hadn’t eat dinner with all the commotion. It really put our minds at ease.

I really appreciate that Dr. Hilfman explained that he would have to go in priority of urgency and our bunny might have to wait for treatment but assured that he would fit him in during his shift and that he would be comfortable in his vet crate. He gave us the option to wait in the lobby or said we go home and sleep if we preferred. We didn’t get a lot of sleep but more than if we had stayed there overnight.

It was clear that Dr. Hilfman and the team on duty overnight really cared about the welfare of our bunny. He is recovering well and we am grateful for how they took care of him.

text.text: We had to visit Dove Lewis this weekend, after leaving a VCA emergency clinic due to lack of care, (search VCA in Clackamas to read my full review) (10-10-25) My doggo was immediately seen ($150 emergency fee) and we were taken to a room to wait. He was assessed and given a  X-ray ($400) within 30 mins of arriving. Thankfully and by God's will, there was no blockage. The Dr that was taking care of my guy sat in the room with us and went over everything they checked and looked at. Her and the techs continued to come in and assess him, walking him up and down the hallway to see if it's bones or absolutely anything else that could be affecting him the way it was (took him up some stairs because the day before he was going up and down the stairs a little funny not wanting to jump up). They did literally everything they could to try to figure out what was wrong with him all while he never left my sight. I am so beyond grateful for their compassion and thorough care. The Dr herself sat in the room with us for over 30 mins just talking and coming up with a game plan, and trying to think of everything she could try to get a idea of what's wrong. At the end with a comprehensive game plan, we were able to leave and went to the front to pay the bill. At this point I'm assuming at least $400 and obviously more for whatever "tests" they had conducted, and the person at the desk said "ok, so it looks like just $134 and you're good to go". They didn't even charge us for the x-ray, I was beside myself. Their generosity and compassion and willingness to help WITHOUT mention of any money, and my guys care not contingent on what money I did or did not have. I was so thankful, my pets are my life and to feel like their quality of care depends on how many hundreds of dollars I had (or in this case didn't have). My youngest daughter is a freshman and she's going to school to become a non profit veterinarian so she can help the animals and people in need and do whatever it takes to make sure everyone is taken care of and ok, this entire event just solidified the reason for her career path, we need so many more people like her and Dove Lewis. Nothing less.

I'm highly disappointed. My first experience here was good and positive and helped my poor girl recover from medications from an ER vet that were making her symptoms worse. Gold star, thank you to the lovely Dr who helped my girl and didn't make me feel like an awful pet parent.

Recently I began work again after a 3 month medical leave and my cat has been adjusting horribly. She made herself sick and as I explained multiple times over the phone and in person regarding my financial situation and what I know she needs, I was told NO payment plans (suggested I sign up for credit care) - The entire experience felt "well if you can't pay your cat will die and oh well." - All because of policy (what kind of vet does that??? Is that a Portland thing??) - then once at the exam, and again going over the issue, I felt pressured in giving her unnecessary tests that cost upwards of $800+. It was back and forth between me and the vet for an hour over hypothetical issues of signs she was not experiencing but "preventative".

Never in my animal care life have I ever experienced anything like this from a vet. Maybe it's just where I'm from, but vets I've experienced in the past willingly help your pets and help make a payment plan if you can't fork over the hundreds or thousands of dollars that's requested. My previous vets, the pet comes first and worries about money later. The company feels more about making a quick buck and putting financial burdens on pet parents versus actually caring for the animal. No payment plans, no billing later, pay now or go elsewhere.

She's doing much better now (thank goodness) but I won't be returning or recommending this place.

We have been going to Grateful Heart for about 4 years now, and will (hopefully) never have to change vets. We’ve even moved across town, yet continue making the commute to Grateful Heart because of the exceptional care we receive for our animals.

When our dog Arly was sick and dying of oral cancer, they delivered the news in the most compassionate way they could, and delivered palliative, end-of-life care to make her transition out of this world as smooth as possible. When she passed, they sent us a personalized note from staff acknowledging her passing.

Now we bring our newer pup Java, and they continue to provide excellent care through all of her needs. Java is a German Shepherd, so she sometimes has difficulty with bloodwork, etc.— and they are so mindful to not traumatize her or give her a bad experience that turns her into a reactive pup. They are gentle and kind with her, despite her flight response.

From the techs, to the doctors, to the front desk staff, we could not ask for more patient or caring people tending to our pups’ needs. We’ve seen all of the vets by now, and each has done nothing but exceed our expectations. You can tell when a vet clinic genuinely cares about you, and loves the work that they are doing— and this place exemplifies that. Thank you, Grateful Heart, for doing such a great job! We’d recommend them to anyone. We are grateful!
